title: Portugal among favourites to win Nations League, insists Jesus
subtitle: Portugal finished their Group A4 campaign on a high by edging past Wales and securing top spot ahead of the quarter-finals.
paragraphs: Jorge Jesus says defending champions Portugal are firm contenders to win the Nations League and insists he is not worried about their defensive frailties.
Portugal bounced back from their heavy 4-1 defeat to Denmark last time out to edge Wales in a five-goal thriller, beating Craig Bellamy's side 3-2 despite finishing the game with 10 men.
Bruno Fernandes' opener was swiftly cancelled out by David Brooks, and Portugal pulled back level at half-time, with Pedro Neto equalising after Sorba Thomas had put Wales in front.
Portugal pushed after the break and eventually got the winner through substitute Carlos Forbs – wearing the number seven shirt that has been vacated by Cristiano Ronaldo.
They then held on after Neto received two bookings in quick succession, ensuring they finished top of Group A4, having already secured their qualification for the quarter-finals.
Jesus is confident Portugal will be challenging for the title again this time around, though he noted the knockouts will be no easy feat.
"The first objective was qualification. Then, to be first. We got 15 points; England and Spain did too," he said.
"[Portugal are] a contender because we've already won twice. We're already in the quarter-finals; let's see who we get in the draw.
"In the Nations League group stage, you play against great European teams; in a European Championship, you play against teams that... have nothing to do with the Nations League.
"Let's see who we get. I'm not worried. The strong sometimes become weaker and the weaker, strong."
While Portugal won five of their group games, they looked shaky during this international break and faced 22 shots from Wales, who were already confirmed in fourth place prior to the game.
The Dragons managed double the total Portugal did, and got eight of their attempts on target, accumulating 1.8 expected goals (xG).
But Jesus was not concerned with the number of chances they faced, noting that Portugal limited their hosts to long-range efforts.
"No. I'm worried about the eight shots inside the penalty area. We had six," he added.
"Given the timing of Pedro Neto's sending-off, the team defended very deep in the 3-2 situation, and the Welsh team had many shots from outside the area.
"Our team, inside the penalty area, defending the result, meant that Wales had more shots than usual."

Portugal bounced back from their heavy 4-1 defeat to Denmark last time out to edge Wales in a five-goal thriller, beating Craig Bellamy's side 3-2 despite finishing the game with 10 men.

Bruno Fernandes' opener was swiftly cancelled out by David Brooks, and Portugal pulled back level at half-time, with Pedro Neto equalising after Sorba Thomas had put Wales in front.

They then held on after Neto received two bookings in quick succession, ensuring they finished top of Group A4, having already secured their qualification for the quarter-finals.

Jesus is confident Portugal will be challenging for the title again this time around, though he noted the knockouts will be no easy feat.

"The first objective was qualification. Then, to be first. We got 15 points; England and Spain did too," he said.

"[Portugal are] a contender because we've already won twice. We're already in the quarter-finals; let's see who we get in the draw.

"In the Nations League group stage, you play against great European teams; in a European Championship, you play against teams that... have nothing to do with the Nations League.

While Portugal won five of their group games, they looked shaky during this international break and faced 22 shots from Wales, who were already confirmed in fourth place prior to the game.

The Dragons managed double the total Portugal did, and got eight of their attempts on target, accumulating 1.8 expected goals (xG).
